review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

16:1.sourceText: Κατήντησεν δὲ καὶ εἰς Δέρβην καὶ εἰς Λύστραν. καὶ ἰδοὺ μαθητής τις ἦν ἐκεῖ ὀνόματι Τιμόθεος, υἱὸς γυναικὸς Ἰουδαίας πιστῆς πατρὸς δὲ Ἕλληνος,
16:1.targetText: Paul came to Derbe and then to Lystra, where he found a disciple named Timothy, the son of a believing Jewish woman and a Greek father.

groups.note: ἰδοὺ … ἦν ("behold, there was"), which brings in Timothy, is rendered he found.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated.
BSB leaves καί ("also") untranslated.
BSB joins this clause to the last with where, leaving καί unrendered.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; the Greek has only the verb ending.

16:2.sourceText: ὃς ἐμαρτυρεῖτο ὑπὸ τῶν ἐν Λύστροις καὶ Ἰκονίῳ ἀδελφῶν.
16:2.targetText: The brothers in Lystra and Iconium spoke well of him.

groups.note: The relative ὅς ("who") is rendered him, the object of BSB's active verb.
The passive ἐμαρτυρεῖτο ("he was well spoken of") is rendered as an active, spoke well of.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB turns the passive into an active, so ὑπό ("by") has no English word.

16:3.sourceText: τοῦτον ἠθέλησεν ὁ Παῦλος σὺν αὐτῷ ἐξελθεῖν, καὶ λαβὼν περιέτεμεν αὐτὸν διὰ τοὺς Ἰουδαίους τοὺς ὄντας ἐν τοῖς τόποις ἐκείνοις· ᾔδεισαν γὰρ ἅπαντες ὅτι Ἕλλην ὁ πατὴρ αὐτοῦ ὑπῆρχεν.
16:3.targetText: Paul wanted Timothy to accompany him, so he took him and circumcised him on account of the Jews in that area, for they all knew that his father was a Greek.

groups.note: The pronoun τοῦτον ("this one") is rendered Timothy.
σὺν … ἐξελθεῖν ("to go out with") is rendered to accompany.
The one object αὐτόν serves λαβών and περιέτεμεν; BSB gives him with both.
τόποις ("places") is rendered area.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB renders τοὺς ὄντας ἐν ("who were in") with the preposition alone.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the participle λαβών, rendered took, to the main verb circumcised.

16:4.sourceText: Ὡς δὲ διεπορεύοντο τὰς πόλεις, παρεδίδοσαν αὐτοῖς φυλάσσειν τὰ δόγματα τὰ κεκριμένα ὑπὸ τῶν ἀποστόλων καὶ πρεσβυτέρων τῶν ἐν Ἱεροσολύμοις.
16:4.targetText: As they went from town to town, they delivered the decisions handed down by the apostles and elders in Jerusalem for the people to obey.

groups.note: τὰς πόλεις ("the towns") is rendered from town to town.
αὐτοῖς ("to them") is rendered for the people, the subject of to obey.
The article with the participle κεκριμένα ("those decided") is rendered handed down.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB renders τῶν ἐν ("those in") with the preposition alone.

16:5.sourceText: Αἱ μὲν οὖν ἐκκλησίαι ἐστερεοῦντο τῇ πίστει καὶ ἐπερίσσευον τῷ ἀριθμῷ καθ’ ἡμέραν.
16:5.targetText: So the churches were strengthened in the faith and grew daily in numbers.

groups.note: καθ’ ἡμέραν ("day by day") is rendered daily.

unmappedSource.reason: The particle μέν, answered by no δέ here, has no English counterpart.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

16:6.sourceText: Διῆλθον δὲ τὴν Φρυγίαν καὶ Γαλατικὴν χώραν, κωλυθέντες ὑπὸ τοῦ Ἁγίου Πνεύματος λαλῆσαι τὸν λόγον ἐν τῇ Ἀσίᾳ·
16:6.targetText: After the Holy Spirit had prevented them from speaking the word in the province of Asia, they traveled through the region of Phrygia and Galatia.

groups.note: The passive κωλυθέντες ("having been prevented") is rendered as an active, After … had prevented them.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated.
BSB turns the passive into an active, so ὑπό ("by") has no English word.

unmappedTarget.reason: BSB adds that Asia was a Roman province.

16:7.sourceText: ἐλθόντες δὲ κατὰ τὴν Μυσίαν ἐπείραζον εἰς τὴν Βιθυνίαν πορευθῆναι, καὶ οὐκ εἴασεν αὐτοὺς τὸ Πνεῦμα Ἰησοῦ·
16:7.targetText: And when they came to the border of Mysia, they tried to enter Bithynia, but the Spirit of Jesus would not permit them.

groups.note: κατά ("down to, opposite") with Mysia is rendered to the border of.
εἰς … πορευθῆναι ("to go into") is rendered to enter.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

16:8.sourceText: παρελθόντες δὲ τὴν Μυσίαν κατέβησαν εἰς Τρῳάδα.
16:8.targetText: So they passed by Mysia and went down to Troas.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the participle παρελθόντες, rendered passed by, to the main verb went down.

16:9.sourceText: καὶ ὅραμα διὰ νυκτὸς τῷ Παύλῳ ὤφθη, ἀνὴρ Μακεδών τις ἦν ἑστὼς καὶ παρακαλῶν αὐτὸν καὶ λέγων Διαβὰς εἰς Μακεδονίαν βοήθησον ἡμῖν.
16:9.targetText: During the night, Paul had a vision of a man of Macedonia standing and pleading with him, “Come over to Macedonia and help us.”

groups.note: ὤφθη ("appeared") to Paul is rendered Paul had.
The periphrastic ἦν ἑστώς ("was standing") is rendered standing.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening καί untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves καὶ λέγων ("and saying") unexpressed before the quotation.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the man to the vision with of; the Greek describes him in a new clause.
English joins the participle Διαβάς, rendered Come over, to the main verb help.

16:10.sourceText: ὡς δὲ τὸ ὅραμα εἶδεν, εὐθέως ἐζητήσαμεν ἐξελθεῖν εἰς Μακεδονίαν, συμβιβάζοντες ὅτι προσκέκληται ἡμᾶς ὁ Θεὸς εὐαγγελίσασθαι αὐτούς.
16:10.targetText: As soon as Paul had seen the vision, we got ready to leave for Macedonia, concluding that God had called us to preach the gospel to them.

groups.note: ὡς … εὐθέως ("when … immediately") is rendered As soon as.
ἐζητήσαμεν ("we sought") is rendered we got ready.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; the Greek has only the verb ending.

16:11.sourceText: Ἀναχθέντες δὲ ἀπὸ Τρῳάδος εὐθυδρομήσαμεν εἰς Σαμοθρᾴκην, τῇ δὲ ἐπιούσῃ εἰς Νέαν Πόλιν,
16:11.targetText: We sailed from Troas straight to Samothrace, and the following day on to Neapolis.

groups.note: The participle Ἀναχθέντες ("having put out to sea") is rendered sailed.
εὐθυδρομήσαμεν ("we ran a straight course") is rendered We … straight.
ἐπιούσῃ ("the next", with day understood) is rendered following day.
Νέαν Πόλιν ("New City") is the name Neapolis.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated.

16:12.sourceText: κἀκεῖθεν εἰς Φιλίππους, ἥτις ἐστὶν πρώτη τῆς μερίδος Μακεδονίας πόλις, κολωνία. Ἦμεν δὲ ἐν ταύτῃ τῇ πόλει διατρίβοντες ἡμέρας τινάς.
16:12.targetText: From there we went to the Roman colony of Philippi, the leading city of that district of Macedonia. And we stayed there several days.

groups.note: κἀκεῖθεν ("and from there") is rendered From there.
The article τῆς is rendered that.
The periphrastic Ἦμεν … διατρίβοντες ("we were spending time") is rendered we stayed.
ἐν ταύτῃ τῇ πόλει ("in this city") is rendered there.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB turns the relative clause ἥτις ἐστίν ("which is") into an apposition.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a verb and its subject; the Greek continues the sentence of 16:11 (we sailed straight …) without a new verb.

16:13.sourceText: τῇ τε ἡμέρᾳ τῶν σαββάτων ἐξήλθομεν ἔξω τῆς πύλης παρὰ ποταμὸν οὗ ἐνομίζομεν προσευχὴν εἶναι, καὶ καθίσαντες ἐλαλοῦμεν ταῖς συνελθούσαις γυναιξίν.
16:13.targetText: On the Sabbath we went outside the city gate along the river, where it was customary to find a place of prayer. After sitting down, we spoke to the women who had gathered there.

groups.note: τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῶν σαββάτων ("on the day of the Sabbaths") is rendered On the Sabbath.
ἐνομίζομεν ("we supposed, we were accustomed") is rendered it was customary.
εἶναι ("to be") is rendered to find.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective τε untranslated.
BSB starts a new sentence here and leaves καί unrendered.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds there; συνελθούσαις ("who had come together") has no word for the place.

16:14.sourceText: καί τις γυνὴ ὀνόματι Λυδία, πορφυρόπωλις πόλεως Θυατείρων, σεβομένη τὸν Θεόν, ἤκουεν, ἧς ὁ Κύριος διήνοιξεν τὴν καρδίαν προσέχειν τοῖς λαλουμένοις ὑπὸ Παύλου.
16:14.targetText: Among those listening was a woman named Lydia, a dealer in purple cloth from the city of Thyatira, who was a worshiper of God. The Lord opened her heart to respond to Paul’s message.

groups.note: ἤκουεν ("was listening") is rendered Among those listening was.
τοῖς λαλουμένοις ("the things being spoken") is rendered message.
ὑπὸ Παύλου ("by Paul") is rendered Paul's.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening καί untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

16:15.sourceText: ὡς δὲ ἐβαπτίσθη καὶ ὁ οἶκος αὐτῆς, παρεκάλεσεν λέγουσα Εἰ κεκρίκατέ με πιστὴν τῷ Κυρίῳ εἶναι, εἰσελθόντες εἰς τὸν οἶκόν μου μένετε· καὶ παρεβιάσατο ἡμᾶς.
16:15.targetText: And when she and her household had been baptized, she urged us, “If you consider me a believer in the Lord, come and stay at my house.” And she persuaded us.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The participle λέγουσα ("saying") is represented only by the comma before the speech.
BSB leaves εἶναι ("to be") unexpressed in you consider me a believer.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the object of urged; παρεκάλεσεν has none.
English joins the participle εἰσελθόντες, rendered come, to the main verb stay.

16:16.sourceText: Ἐγένετο δὲ πορευομένων ἡμῶν εἰς τὴν προσευχὴν, παιδίσκην τινὰ ἔχουσαν πνεῦμα Πύθωνα ὑπαντῆσαι ἡμῖν, ἥτις ἐργασίαν πολλὴν παρεῖχεν τοῖς κυρίοις αὐτῆς μαντευομένη.
16:16.targetText: One day as we were going to the place of prayer, we were met by a slave girl with a spirit of divination, who earned a large income for her masters by fortune-telling.

groups.note: The narrative formula Ἐγένετο δέ ("now it came about") is rendered One day.
Πύθωνα ("of Python") names a spirit of divination.
The active ὑπαντῆσαι ("to meet") is rendered as a passive, we were met by.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

16:17.sourceText: αὕτη κατακολουθοῦσα τῷ Παύλῳ καὶ ἡμῖν ἔκραζεν λέγουσα Οὗτοι οἱ ἄνθρωποι δοῦλοι τοῦ Θεοῦ τοῦ Ὑψίστου εἰσίν, οἵτινες καταγγέλλουσιν ὑμῖν ὁδὸν σωτηρίας.
16:17.targetText: This girl followed Paul and the rest of us, shouting, “These men are servants of the Most High God, who are proclaiming to you the way of salvation!”

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The participle λέγουσα ("saying") is represented only by the comma before the speech.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds the rest of; the Greek says Paul and us.

16:18.sourceText: τοῦτο δὲ ἐποίει ἐπὶ πολλὰς ἡμέρας. διαπονηθεὶς δὲ Παῦλος καὶ ἐπιστρέψας τῷ πνεύματι εἶπεν Παραγγέλλω σοι ἐν ὀνόματι Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ ἐξελθεῖν ἀπ’ αὐτῆς· καὶ ἐξῆλθεν αὐτῇ τῇ ὥρᾳ.
16:18.targetText: She continued this for many days. Eventually Paul grew so aggravated that he turned and said to the spirit, “In the name of Jesus Christ I command you to come out of her!” And the spirit left her at that very moment.

groups.note: διαπονηθείς ("greatly annoyed") is rendered grew so aggravated.
BSB renders καί, joining the two participles, as a result clause (that he turned).
In αὐτῇ τῇ ὥρᾳ ("in the very hour") the article is rendered that.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the participle ἐπιστρέψας, rendered turned, to the main verb said.
English names the subject; the Greek has only the verb ending.
English supplies the object of left; ἐξῆλθεν has none here.

16:19.sourceText: Ἰδόντες δὲ οἱ κύριοι αὐτῆς ὅτι ἐξῆλθεν ἡ ἐλπὶς τῆς ἐργασίας αὐτῶν, ἐπιλαβόμενοι τὸν Παῦλον καὶ τὸν Σιλᾶν εἵλκυσαν εἰς τὴν ἀγορὰν ἐπὶ τοὺς ἄρχοντας,
16:19.targetText: When the girl’s owners saw that their hope of making money was gone, they seized Paul and Silas and dragged them before the authorities in the marketplace.

groups.note: αὐτῆς ("her") is rendered the girl's.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the participle ἐπιλαβόμενοι, rendered seized, to the main verb dragged.
English supplies the object of dragged; the Greek names Paul and Silas once, with ἐπιλαβόμενοι.

16:20.sourceText: καὶ προσαγαγόντες αὐτοὺς τοῖς στρατηγοῖς εἶπαν Οὗτοι οἱ ἄνθρωποι ἐκταράσσουσιν ἡμῶν τὴν πόλιν, Ἰουδαῖοι ὑπάρχοντες,
16:20.targetText: They brought them to the magistrates and said, “These men are Jews and are throwing our city into turmoil

unmappedSource.reason: BSB starts a new sentence here and leaves καί unrendered.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the participle προσαγαγόντες, rendered brought, to the main verb said.
English joins the participle phrase Ἰουδαῖοι ὑπάρχοντες, rendered are Jews, to the main verb.

16:21.sourceText: καὶ καταγγέλλουσιν ἔθη ἃ οὐκ ἔξεστιν ἡμῖν παραδέχεσθαι οὐδὲ ποιεῖν Ῥωμαίοις οὖσιν.
16:21.targetText: by promoting customs that are unlawful for us Romans to adopt or practice.”

groups.note: BSB renders καί, adding the second charge, as by.
οὐκ ἔξεστιν ("it is not lawful") is rendered are unlawful.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves οὖσιν ("being") unexpressed in us Romans.

16:22.sourceText: καὶ συνεπέστη ὁ ὄχλος κατ’ αὐτῶν, καὶ οἱ στρατηγοὶ περιρήξαντες αὐτῶν τὰ ἱμάτια ἐκέλευον ῥαβδίζειν,
16:22.targetText: The crowd joined in the attack against Paul and Silas, and the magistrates ordered that they be stripped and beaten with rods.

groups.note: αὐτῶν ("them") is rendered Paul and Silas.
περιρήξαντες … τὰ ἱμάτια ("having torn off the garments") is rendered be stripped.
αὐτῶν ("their" garments) is rendered they, the subject of be stripped.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB starts a new sentence here and leaves καί unrendered.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the participle περιρήξαντες, rendered be stripped, to the infinitive beaten.

16:23.sourceText: πολλάς δὲ ἐπιθέντες αὐτοῖς πληγὰς ἔβαλον εἰς φυλακήν, παραγγείλαντες τῷ δεσμοφύλακι ἀσφαλῶς τηρεῖν αὐτούς·
16:23.targetText: And after striking them with many blows, they threw them into prison and ordered the jailer to guard them securely.

groups.note: BSB's Greek text has a different connective here, with the same sense.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the object of threw; αὐτοῖς is the dative of ἐπιθέντες, and ἔβαλον has no object of its own.
English joins the participle παραγγείλαντες, rendered ordered, to the main verb threw.

16:24.sourceText: ὃς παραγγελίαν τοιαύτην λαβὼν ἔβαλεν αὐτοὺς εἰς τὴν ἐσωτέραν φυλακὴν καὶ τοὺς πόδας ἠσφαλίσατο αὐτῶν εἰς τὸ ξύλον.
16:24.targetText: On receiving this order, he placed them in the inner cell and fastened their feet in the stocks.

groups.note: The relative ὅς ("who") is rendered he, as BSB starts a new sentence.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

16:25.sourceText: Κατὰ δὲ τὸ μεσονύκτιον Παῦλος καὶ Σιλᾶς προσευχόμενοι ὕμνουν τὸν Θεόν, ἐπηκροῶντο δὲ αὐτῶν οἱ δέσμιοι·
16:25.targetText: About midnight Paul and Silas were praying and singing hymns to God, and the other prisoners were listening to them.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the participle προσευχόμενοι, rendered were praying, to the main verb singing hymns.
English adds other to set the prisoners apart from Paul and Silas.

16:26.sourceText: ἄφνω δὲ σεισμὸς ἐγένετο μέγας, ὥστε σαλευθῆναι τὰ θεμέλια τοῦ δεσμωτηρίου· ἠνεῴχθησαν δὲ παραχρῆμα αἱ θύραι πᾶσαι, καὶ πάντων τὰ δεσμὰ ἀνέθη.
16:26.targetText: Suddenly a strong earthquake shook the foundations of the prison. At once all the doors flew open and everyone’s chains came loose.

groups.note: The passive σαλευθῆναι ("to be shaken") is rendered as an active, shook.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated.
BSB turns "a great earthquake happened, so that the foundations were shaken" into one clause; ἐγένετο ("happened") and ὥστε ("so that") have no English word.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

16:27.sourceText: ἔξυπνος δὲ γενόμενος ὁ δεσμοφύλαξ καὶ ἰδὼν ἀνεῳγμένας τὰς θύρας τῆς φυλακῆς, σπασάμενος τὴν μάχαιραν ἤμελλεν ἑαυτὸν ἀναιρεῖν, νομίζων ἐκπεφευγέναι τοὺς δεσμίους.
16:27.targetText: When the jailer woke up and saw the prison doors open, he drew his sword and was about to kill himself, presuming that the prisoners had escaped.

groups.note: ἔξυπνος γενόμενος ("having become awake") is rendered When … woke up.
The article τήν serves as the possessive.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the participle σπασάμενος, rendered drew, to the main verb was about.

16:28.sourceText: ἐφώνησεν δὲ Παῦλος μεγάλῃ φωνῇ λέγων Μηδὲν πράξῃς σεαυτῷ κακόν, ἅπαντες γάρ ἐσμεν ἐνθάδε.
16:28.targetText: But Paul called out in a loud voice, “Do not harm yourself! We are all here!”

unmappedSource.reason: The participle λέγων ("saying") is represented only by the comma before the speech.
BSB leaves γάρ ("for") untranslated and gives the reason as its own sentence.

16:29.sourceText: αἰτήσας δὲ φῶτα εἰσεπήδησεν καὶ ἔντρομος γενόμενος προσέπεσεν τῷ Παύλῳ καὶ Σιλᾷ,
16:29.targetText: Calling for lights, the jailer rushed in and fell trembling before Paul and Silas.

groups.note: ἔντρομος γενόμενος ("having become trembling") is rendered trembling.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; the Greek has only the verb ending.

16:30.sourceText: καὶ προαγαγὼν αὐτοὺς ἔξω ἔφη Κύριοι, τί με δεῖ ποιεῖν ἵνα σωθῶ;
16:30.targetText: Then he brought them out and asked, “Sirs, what must I do to be saved?”

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the participle προαγαγών, rendered brought, to the main verb asked.

16:31.sourceText: οἱ δὲ εἶπαν Πίστευσον ἐπὶ τὸν Κύριον Ἰησοῦν, καὶ σωθήσῃ σὺ καὶ ὁ οἶκός σου.
16:31.targetText: They replied, “Believe in the Lord Jesus and you will be saved, you and your household.”

groups.note: The article οἱ is used as a pronoun ("they").

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

16:32.sourceText: καὶ ἐλάλησαν αὐτῷ τὸν λόγον τοῦ Θεοῦ σὺν πᾶσιν τοῖς ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ αὐτοῦ.
16:32.targetText: Then Paul and Silas spoke the word of the Lord to him and to everyone in his house.

groups.note: σύν ("with") is rendered and to, joining everyone to him.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB follows a reading with a different word here; its English says Lord where N1904 has Θεοῦ ("God").
BSB renders τοῖς ἐν ("those in") with the preposition alone.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; the Greek has only the verb ending.
Goes with Lord: BSB follows a reading with a different word here, where N1904 has Θεοῦ ("of God").
BSB follows a reading with a different word here; N1904 has Θεοῦ ("God").

16:33.sourceText: καὶ παραλαβὼν αὐτοὺς ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ὥρᾳ τῆς νυκτὸς ἔλουσεν ἀπὸ τῶν πληγῶν, καὶ ἐβαπτίσθη αὐτὸς καὶ οἱ αὐτοῦ ἅπαντες παραχρῆμα,
16:33.targetText: At that hour of the night, the jailer took them and washed their wounds. And without delay, he and all his household were baptized.

groups.note: The article τῶν serves as the possessive.
οἱ αὐτοῦ ("those of his") is rendered his household.
BSB's Greek text has another form of this word here, with the same meaning.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB opens the sentence with the time phrase and leaves καί unrendered.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB says washed their wounds, so ἀπό ("from") has no English word.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; the Greek has only the participle.
English joins the participle παραλαβών, rendered took, to the main verb washed.

16:34.sourceText: ἀναγαγών τε αὐτοὺς εἰς τὸν οἶκον παρέθηκεν τράπεζαν, καὶ ἠγαλλιάσατο πανοικεὶ πεπιστευκὼς τῷ Θεῷ.
16:34.targetText: Then he brought them into his home and set a meal before them. So he and all his household rejoiced that they had come to believe in God.

groups.note: The article τόν serves as the possessive.
παρέθηκεν ("set before") is rendered set … before.
τράπεζαν ("a table") is rendered a meal.
πανοικεί ("with the whole household") is rendered and all his household.

targetPhrases.text: that they had come to believe

groups.note: The singular πεπιστευκώς ("having believed") is rendered that they had come to believe, including the household.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the participle ἀναγαγών, rendered brought, to the main verb set.
English supplies whom the meal was set before; παρέθηκεν has no dative here.

16:35.targetText: When daylight came, the magistrates sent their officers with the order: “Release those men.”

16:37.sourceText: ὁ δὲ Παῦλος ἔφη πρὸς αὐτούς Δείραντες ἡμᾶς δημοσίᾳ ἀκατακρίτους, ἀνθρώπους Ῥωμαίους ὑπάρχοντας, ἔβαλαν εἰς φυλακήν· καὶ νῦν λάθρᾳ ἡμᾶς ἐκβάλλουσιν; οὐ γάρ, ἀλλὰ ἐλθόντες αὐτοὶ ἡμᾶς ἐξαγαγέτωσαν.
16:37.targetText: But Paul said to the officers, “They beat us publicly without a trial and threw us into prison, even though we are Roman citizens. And now do they want to send us away secretly? Absolutely not! Let them come themselves and escort us out!”

groups.note: αὐτούς ("them") is rendered the officers.

The present ἐκβάλλουσιν ("are they sending out") is rendered do they want to send … away.

The participle ἐλθόντες ("having come") is rendered come.
The imperative ἐξαγαγέτωσαν ("let them lead out") is rendered Let them … escort … out.
